result:
I graded submission s1 for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s1.json`. Riley got 2 of 6 items fully correct, 2 partial and 2 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | wrong (M4) | Riley chose "the model opens the booking system itself". The model only writes a tool request. The program runs the tool. |
| q3 | correct | A step limit is the right safeguard against a repeating loop. |
| q4 | wrong (M4) | Riley answered 1, as if the model ran all three tools in one call. The answer is 4: one call per tool request, plus one for the final answer. |
| q5 | partial | "Sends it back to the model" is right, but the answer leaves out why. The model needs the result in its next input to choose its next step or write the answer. |
| q6 | partial (M3) | Riley was right that the model picks tools from their descriptions. Riley was wrong that it "remembers on its own" from earlier sessions. The program has to supply any memory. |

**Summary:** Riley has the loop, the need for a stopping condition, and tool choice from descriptions. The weak point is who does what. The model only writes text, including its tool requests. The program runs the tools and calls the model again at every step.

I also added `learning-records/0003-who-runs-the-tools.md` for the open M4 and M3 misconceptions, and updated `NOTES.md`.

**Next step for Riley:** Redo the trace "Is the laser cutter free tomorrow at 3 pm, and do I need training?" as a two-column table, "model writes" and "program does". Then count the model calls. After that, the context and memory topic can start from a firm base. Submission s2 is still ungraded.
